item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 10, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
China News Service: Zoo Atlanta has held the inauguration of the new panda grove, marking the public debut of giant pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang. Does China have any comment? Guo Jiakun: On September 24, during his state visit to the United States, President Xi Jinping announced that two giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, would soon find their new home in Zoo Atlanta, which was warmly welcomed by people in the U.S. On September 27 local time, the two pandas arrived in Atlanta. We are happy to see that the duo have recently made their public debut, bringing great joy to the local people and strengthening the bonds of friendship between the Chinese and American peoples. The giant panda is China’s national treasure and an envoy of friendship. To ensure the pair’s health and safety as well as smooth journey and adaptation to the new environment, thorough preparations have been made in strict accordance with the requirements and technical standards for international giant panda conservation cooperation. We believe this new panda cooperation will benefit the protection of giant pandas and other endangered species, global biodiversity conservation, and people-to-people friendship between China and the U.S. AFP: This is a question regarding the allegations that tech executive Alice Huang was working for Chinese intelligence as she had a close relationship with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. So my question is, does the Chinese leader plan to address these spying allegations with Donald Trump? Guo Jiakun: On the meeting between Chinese and U.S. presidents, the two sides are in communication regarding interactions between the two heads of state within the year. On the so-called “Chinese spy,” we’ve stated China’s position on multiple occasions. Bloomberg: Could the foreign ministry confirm whether Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen and what her current whereabouts are? Guo Jiakun: We responded to that yesterday. The “Chinese spy” allegation is purely unsubstantiated and directed at smearing China. AFP: According to reports by the Wall Street Journal, the Chinese leader would not be willing to participate in a trilateral with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of APEC if the talks allow for open discussion of issues including nuclear arms control, as opposed to determining the outcomes ahead of time. Would China like to comment and what are China’s hopes for the trilateral meeting? Guo Jiakun: China is in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state. As to your specific question, I have no information to offer at the moment.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 9, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
Special Envoy of the Communist Party of Cuba (PCC) and the Cuban Government, Member of the Political Bureau of the PCC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla will pay an official visit to China from November 10 to 13. At the invitation of Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi, Slovakia’s Minister of Foreign and European Affairs Juraj Blanár will visit China from November 10 to 11. Xinhua News Agency: According to reports, a Pakistani astronaut will join the Shenzhou XXIV mission crew as payload specialist and complete a short orbital flight before returning to Earth with the Shenzhou XXIII spaceship. I wonder if you have any comment on this? Guo Jiakun: Exploration of the vast universe and peaceful use of outer space are humanity’s shared pursuit and bear on the welfare of all peoples. China advocates the peaceful use of outer space, engages in active international space cooperation, and promotes the building of a community with a shared future in the domain of outer space. China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners. Having the Pakistani astronaut on board China’s spaceships will mark the first ever joint mission of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China’s manned space program. The Pakistani astronaut will be the first foreign astronaut to step into China’s space station. This is yet another key outcome of bilateral cooperation as we mark the 75th anniversary of China-Pakistan diplomatic ties. We stand ready to work with the Pakistani side to carry forward our traditional friendship, deepen cooperation in space and other fields, and bring bilateral relations to new heights. CCTV: Can you provide more details about the visit by Special Envoy of the PCC and Government of Cuba, Member of the Political Bureau of the PCC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla? Guo Jiakun: China and Cuba are good friends, good comrades and good brothers. The upcoming visit by Special Envoy Rodríguez speaks volumes about the high political mutual trust between our two countries. China attaches great importance to this visit. We look forward to an in-depth exchange of views on China-Cuba relations and issues of mutual interest, and will work with the Cuban side to further implement the important common understandings reached between our two leaders, strengthen communication and coordination, deepen exchanges and cooperation across the board, and continue building a China-Cuba community with a shared future. AFP: Chip giant NVIDIA’s board has opened a probe into Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman U.S. officials say was working for Chinese intelligence. This comes after reports from The New York Times and the Financial Times linking Jensen Huang to a Chinese citizen and tech executive. Can the Chinese foreign ministry comment on this? (Similar question from NBC) Guo Jiakun: We responded to that last week. The “Chinese spy” allegation is purely unsubstantiated and directed at smearing China. Beijing Youth Daily: To follow up on the announcement of Slovak Foreign Minister Blanár’s visit to China, how does China view its relations with Slovakia? What’s China’s expectation of this visit? Guo Jiakun: China and Slovakia enjoy traditional friendship. In recent years, under the strategic guidance of the leaders of the two countries, China-Slovakia relations have made marked progress. In particular, since China-Slovakia strategic partnership was established in 2024, solid progress has been made in deepening exchanges and cooperation in various fields. In July this year, Slovak President Pellegrini paid a state visit to China. President Xi Jinping held talks with him to jointly draw a blueprint for the future development of bilateral relations. China will work with Slovakia to carry forward traditional friendship, deepen political mutual trust, expand practical cooperation, strive for solid progress in advancing high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and cooperation between China and Central and Eastern European countries, and sustain the strong momentum of bilateral relations. AFP: U.S. President Donald Trump said he would likely be meeting with the leaders of Russia and China next week in Shenzhen to discuss ending the Iran war as well as other topics like denuclearization. Can the foreign ministry comment on this or offer us any additional details on the agenda of the meeting with Trump and Putin? Guo Jiakun: China maintains communication with the relevant parties on the meeting between the three presidents. As for your specific question, I have no information to offer at the moment. CGTN: Austrian Federal Chancellor Christian Stocker recently paid an official visit to China. How does China see the outcomes of the visit and how do you envision the future development of China-Austria relations? Guo Jiakun: This year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Austria. As a highlight in the commemoration program, Federal Chancellor Christian Stocker paid a successful visit to China and attended the ninth China International Import Expo. During Chancellor Stocker’s stay in Beijing, President Xi Jinping met with him and Premier Li Qiang and Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee Zhao Leji held talks and met with him respectively. The leaders had in-depth exchanges of views on bilateral ties and China-EU relations as well as international and regional issues of mutual interest. Both sides agreed to carry forward the traditional friendship between the two countries, respect each other’s core interests, sustain the positive momentum in high-level exchanges, deepen mutually beneficial practical cooperation in such fields as economy, trade, culture, science and technology and at the sub-national level on the basis of mutual trust, and strengthen coordination at the UN Security Council and other multilateral platforms to jointly support multilateralism. During the visit, Premier Li and Chancellor Stocker witnessed the signing of three documents on cooperation in economy, trade, social security and other areas, which serves to consolidate the foundation of bilateral ties and illustrate what can be achieved if China and the EU see each other as partners and tap into the potential for cooperation. The Paper: We noticed that the Standing Committee of the 14th National People’s Congress decided at its 25th Meeting to ratify the Agreement on the Establishment of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO). Could you share more information on that? Guo Jiakun: In July this year, at the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance, President Xi Jinping announced that WAICO had come into being. The initiative has received positive response from the international community, with 38 countries as the founding members. As the initiator and the host country of WAICO, China is now taking the lead to ratify the Agreement on the Establishment of WAICO. That demonstrates China’s genuine aspiration and firm commitment to getting the organization up and running. Guided by the vision of extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit, China will make continuous efforts to promote the physical operation of WAICO, and focus on the practical cooperation and capacity building in the Global South, so that all countries can share the opportunities and dividends brought by AI. We welcome and expect more countries to join WAICO, to promote global AI development for good and for all, and to jointly build a just and equitable global AI governance system. AFP: Reuters reported that about 600,000 of NVIDIA’s advanced AI chips are stored in Hong Kong. The chips are awaiting shipment to mainland China as Beijing withholds approval for large scale imports despite demand from tech firms. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on this report? Guo Jiakun: China’s position on the U.S. export of chips to China is consistent. For anything specific, I’d refer you to competent authorities. RIA Novosti: Earlier, Washington Post columnist David Ignatius reported citing sources, that the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump has asked China to help bring an end to the conflict with Iran. Could you please confirm this? Guo Jiakun: To prolong the conflict between the U.S. and Iran does not serve the common interest of the parties concerned and the international community. Relevant parties should stick to peace, resolve disputes through dialogue and negotiation, and restore peace and tranquility in the Middle East and Gulf region at an early date. Bloomberg: Jensen Huang has been an advocate for looser policy and selling more chips to China. And the Democrats have also just won the Congress and may have a different approach to tech curbs. How will China respond if the U.S. pushes for tighter tech curbs, including on chips? Guo Jiakun: As I just said, China’s position on the U.S. export of chips to China is consistent. For anything specific, I’d refer you to competent authorities. ***************************************** The following question was raised by Reuters after the press conference: Taiwan’s so-called “foreign affairs office” announced on November 6 the closure of the “Taipei Economic Office” in Port Moresby, and that “no new spot contracts” for the purchases of liquefied natural gas will be signed with Papua New Guinea. Taiwan also said that Papua New Guinea renewed its unilateral demands for personnel of the “office” to leave the country within a specified timeframe and for the “office” to be shut down. What is China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: The decision by the government of Papua New Guinea to close the “Taipei Economic Office” in Papua New Guinea once again shows that upholding the one-China principle is where international public opinion trends and the arc of history bends. China appreciates this and will continue working with Papua New Guinea to firmly support each other’s core interests and major concerns. China stands ready to increase imports of liquefied natural gas from Papua New Guinea, deepen cooperation in economy and trade and other areas, and add new dimensions to our comprehensive strategic partnership.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 6, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
As agreed between China and Canada, the second China-Canada Economic and Financial Strategic Dialogue will be held in Canada on November 9. Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Vice Premier of the State Council He Lifeng will co-chair the dialogue as the Chinese lead person with the co-leaders on the Canadian side Minister of Finance and National Revenue Francois-Philippe Champagne and Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu. The Paper: The Ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) and the Hongqiao International Economic Forum Opening Ceremony was held in Shanghai yesterday. The 140th China Import and Export Fair (Canton Fair) also concluded this Wednesday. We have seen media reviews saying that the two expos, held back-to-back, show that China—both the world’s factory and world’s market, both a “super seller” and a “super buyer”—plays an important role in addressing imbalanced trade. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: These expos you mentioned are important windows on China’s global connectedness and how it enables development and delivers for the people across the world. In his keynote speech at the CIIE opening ceremony, Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang noted that the CIIE, since its inception, has witnessed China’s firm resolve and concrete actions to advance high-standard opening up, the tangible outcomes and substantial benefits achieved by businesses and people from all countries in sharing opportunities in the Chinese market, and the unremitting efforts and important contributions of people from all sectors to improving global economic governance. Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang shared four observations on realizing the balance of trade. First, countries should share market opportunities, enhance openness and connectivity, better leverage their respective comparative advantages, and promote balance by making the economic pie bigger together. Second, countries should engage in deeper investment cooperation, make efforts to optimize the cross-border layout of industries, create favorable conditions for businesses, and promote balance through integration into global industrial and supply chains. Third, countries should harness innovation, improve supply quality, expand the frontiers of trade, and promote balance through advancing transformation and upgrading. Fourth, countries should enhance mutual understanding and trust, give due consideration to each other’s legitimate concerns, resolve differences through consultation, and promote balance by removing barriers. China will work with relevant parties to make the CIIE successful, fully leverage the four major platforms of international procurement, investment promotion, people-to-people exchanges, and openness and cooperation, and bring more benefits to the people of countries around the world. Reuters: China has consistently been open to expanding purchases of agricultural goods from the U.S., but only on the condition that the two sides implement their agreed US$30 billion-for-US$30 billion reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement, Commerce Ministry spokesperson said yesterday. Does this mean that China will not begin fulfilling the US$17 billion agriculture pledge until the tariffs are cut? Guo Jiakun: I’d refer you to China’s competent authorities for the specifics. Maintaining the steady development of China-U.S. economic and trade relations is in the interest of both countries and peoples, and conducive to global economic growth. The two sides need to move in the same direction, adhere to mutual benefit and win-win results and promote the continued, steady development and improvement of China-U.S. economic and trade ties. NHK: Tomorrow marks one year since Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi made the comments on Taiwan at the Diet. Does China plan to once again ask the Japanese side to withdraw the comments? What is China’s position on the current and future China-Japan relations? (Similar question from Yomiuri Shimbun) Guo Jiakun: The current serious difficulties in China-Japan relations are entirely the responsibility of the Japanese side. It stems from the erroneous remarks made by the Japanese leader a year ago regarding Taiwan, which blatantly signaled a potential military intervention in the Taiwan question, challenged China’s national sovereignty, and undermined the political foundation of China-Japan relations. Regrettably, one year on, the Japanese authorities have not moved at all. They’ve been evading the issue and yet to demonstrate any sincerity or take any action to reflect upon and correct the wrongdoings. Our position on China-Japan relations has been consistent. We wish to reiterate that for the Japanese side, the pressing priority is to correct the erroneous words and deeds on the Taiwan question, adopt a correct attitude on historical issues, and form an objective and rational perception on China. Xinhua News Agency: A recent Forbes article compared the Africa policies of China and the United States, saying that Washington’s policy has been transactional and narrowed largely to securing key minerals, while China’s philosophy is long-term: build what Africa needs, finance it, and let the host countries govern, thus accumulating influence and enjoying a high rate of recognition. Afrobarometer’s report finds 62 percent of Africans view China’s influence positively. Do you have any comment on this? Guo Jiakun: China and African countries naturally belong to a community with a shared future. China always supports Africa’s efforts to pursue development, revitalization and collective strength under the principles of sincerity, real results, amity and good faith. From May 1 this year, China began the zero-tariff treatment for all 53 African countries having diplomatic ties with China. The policy enables easier access for African agricultural products and light manufactured goods to the Chinese market, and introduces special African products such as avocado, coffee bean, pecan and shea butter to households across China. In the first nine months of this year, China-Africa trade volume exceeded US$310 billion, up by 22 percent year-on-year. This policy has effectively lowered cost for China-Africa trade and brought tangible benefit to more African small and medium-sized enterprises and farmers. No matter how the international landscape might evolve, China is always the most trustworthy and reliable partner for African countries. China-Africa high-quality cooperation will continue boosting both sides’ modernization drive. AFP: In Macao today, a court sentenced former lawmaker Au Kam San to 12.5 years in prison after he was found guilty of working with foreign forces to subvert state authority. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on this? Guo Jiakun: The court of the Macao SAR has released information regarding the sentencing in this case. Let me stress, Macao upholds the rule of law. To abide by the law and bring lawbreakers to justice is a basic principle. No one enjoys any privilege above the law. The Macao SAR has the duty and right to handle in accordance with law suspected acts of colluding with external forces to endanger national security. This is consistent with international law and common international practice, has solid legal basis and is fully justified. The implementation of One Country, Two Systems in Macao since its return has achieved great success recognized by all. The constitutional order based on the Constitution and the Basic Law of the Macao SAR has been firmly established. The SAR’s economy has attained historic leaps and people’s livelihoods have continued to improve amid social harmony and stability. The extensive rights and freedoms Macao residents are entitled to under the Basic Law are fully protected. These are facts there for all to see. The central government firmly supports the Macao SAR in punishing acts and activities endangering national security in accordance with law and firmly opposes any external forces using individual judicial cases to interfere in Macao’s internal affairs and meddle in China’s internal affairs. AFP: Yesterday, the U.S. State Department imposed new sanctions related to Cuba, including on two Chinese companies it accuses of supplying Cuba’s military with electronics and security equipment. Does the foreign ministry have a response to this? Guo Jiakun: China-Cuba cooperation is completely above-board. China stands firmly against illicit unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law and lack UN Security Council authorization, as well as the so-called “long-arm jurisdiction.” We reject attempts by the U.S. side to disrupt and sabotage China-Cuba cooperation and firmly support Cuba in safeguarding national sovereignty and opposing external interference. We will take all measures necessary to resolutely protect the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese businesses. Beijing Daily: According to reports, results of Grenada’s general elections released on November 5 local time show that incumbent Prime Minister Dickon Mitchell is set to secure another term in office. What’s China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: China congratulates Prime Minister Dickon Mitchell on his reelection. Grenada is China’s important cooperation partner in the Caribbean. We stand ready to work with Grenada to further deepen our mutually beneficial and friendly cooperation and deliver more benefits for both peoples.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 5, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
CGTN: The 11th Lancang-Mekong Cooperation (LMC) Foreign Ministers’ Meeting was successfully held yesterday. This important meeting comes on the 10th anniversary of the first LMC Leaders’ Meeting. Can you share more details? Guo Jiakun: Yesterday morning, Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sihasak Phuangketkeow co-chaired the 11th LMC Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Beijing. The six LMC countries took stock of the cooperation outcomes and experience gained. They agreed that over the past decade, LMC has grown with strong momentum in all dimensions, at various levels and in multiple areas, and delivered tangible results beneficial to all. Lancang-Mekong countries are becoming more inter-connected, with more robust growth momentum, stronger security safeguards, and closer people-to-people bonds. Such cooperation has delivered tangibly to the people and boosted the modernization of the six countries. Foreign Minister Wang Yi put forward five proposals for the future development of LMC. First, form new synergy for solidarity and collective strength. The six countries need to carry forward the LMC culture of equality, sincerity, mutual assistance and kinship, and have closer exchanges at all levels and communication on policies. Second, reach new heights of open and win-win cooperation. The six countries need to deepen cooperation along the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, promote regional trade and investment liberalization and facilitation, build the LMC Economic Development Belt, and support more small and smart livelihood programs. Third, foster new driving force through green development and innovation. The six countries need to expand cooperation in emerging areas such as digital economy and artificial intelligence. We welcome more Mekong countries to join the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization. Fourth, enhance security coordination. The six countries need to carry forward the Asian values of peace, cooperation, openness and inclusiveness and the vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security, reject external interference and bloc confrontation, and step up efforts to fight cross-border crimes. Fifth, create new highlights in disaster governance. The six countries need to set up a cross-border cooperation mechanism for disaster warning, and strengthen cooperation in disaster monitoring, early warning and emergency response to improve capability in disaster prevention, mitigation and relief. Foreign Minister Wang Yi stressed that China stands ready to work with Mekong countries in the direction charted by our leaders, take down-to-earth actions to solve problems and improve people’s well-being, and take more effective measures to jointly advance modernization, set LMC as a leading example of regional cooperation and solidarity and collective strength of the Global South, and jointly usher in a new LMC golden decade. Phoenix TV: We have noted that a handful of politicians from the U.S. and other Western countries have repeatedly voiced “concern” over the case against Joshua Wong Chi-fung. Today, a Hong Kong court handed down its sentencing decision on the case of Wong’s collusion conspiracy. Do you have any comment? Guo Jiakun: Hong Kong upholds the rule of law. To abide by the law and bring lawbreakers to justice is a basic principle. Wong Chi-fung is guilty of conspiracy to collude with a foreign country or external elements to endanger national security, and the offence has been found to be of a grave nature. In the face of overwhelming facts and evidence, Wong had no grounds to justify his behavior and pleaded guilty. The central government of China firmly supports the Hong Kong SAR in safeguarding national security and punishing in accordance with the law acts that endanger national security. Relevant parties need to respect China’s sovereignty and the rule of law in Hong Kong, stop making irresponsible remarks on the SAR’s judicial process, and stop interfering in Hong Kong’s judicial affairs and China’s internal affairs in any form. Global Times: It is reported that the Japanese government is set to approve the updated three security documents in December. Sources have said that Japan will continue to position China as its “greatest strategic challenge” in the updated documents, and will nearly double its defense spending over the next five years, with a total reaching 70 trillion to 80 trillion yen. It will focus on stepping up offensive military capabilities such as long-range strikes and unmanned combat. What’s China’s comment on this? Guo Jiakun: Japan’s rapid push to revise the three security documents, boost military expenditure and develop offensive capabilities says a lot about its agenda to speed up remilitarization. The so-called “greatest strategic challenge” is nothing but a pretext for Japan to engage in military expansion in the name of defense. We noted that within Japan there is a growing concern about the distortion of its orientation as a “peace-loving nation” and the severe impact this has had on economy and people’s livelihood. Historically, the Japanese militarists committed horrendous crimes and inflicted immense suffering on people in the Asia Pacific and beyond. The lessons are still fresh and must not be forgotten. Japan’s reckless remilitarization and repeated breach of its “exclusively defense-oriented” policy seriously threaten regional peace and stability, and challenge the postwar international order. The international community must stay on high alert and jointly push back this dangerous tendency. Bloomberg: I was just wondering if you could comment on the state of ties between China and the U.S. following the midterm elections, especially given things like upcoming meetings between the two presidents, the trade truce that’s ongoing until January and stuff like that. Guo Jiakun: We have responded to a similar question. The U.S. midterm elections are a domestic affair. China stands ready to continue working with the U.S. to uphold and deliver on the important common understandings reached by the two heads of state, enhance communication, properly manage differences, expand cooperation, and build a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity. AFP: A Financial Times report said that China has told Japanese investor SoftBank that it will not allow the acquisition of Swiss-Swedish company ABB’s robotics division to go ahead. Can China confirm this or comment on this? Guo Jiakun: I would refer you to the competent Chinese authorities.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on November 4, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
Upon invitation, between November 6 and 12, Vice President Han Zheng will travel to Türkiye to attend the Antalya Leaders’ Summit at the 31st meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change as Special Representative of President Xi Jinping, and visit Georgia. CCTV: To follow up on your announcement that Vice President Han Zheng will travel to Türkiye to attend the Antalya Leaders’ Summit at the 31st meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) as Special Representative of President Xi Jinping, can you share more information and China’s expectation for the summit? Mao Ning: COP31 will soon be held in Antalya, Türkiye. Vice President Han Zheng will attend the Antalya Leaders’ Summit as Special Representative of President Xi Jinping and work with leaders of other countries to provide political guidance for the meeting. The Paris Agreement enters its second decade this year. The meeting will mainly discuss how to strengthen implementation, accelerate action and promote cooperation in the new decade. China stands ready to work with various parties to firmly uphold multilateralism, fully implement the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement, strengthen practical climate action, and contribute to the success of the meeting. The New York Times: What is China’s view of the Congressional elections that just happened in the United States? Do you see any fresh possibilities in U.S.-China relations? Mao Ning: The U.S. midterm elections are a domestic affair. China stands ready to continue working with the U.S. to uphold and deliver on the important common understandings reached by the two heads of state, enhance communication, properly manage differences, expand cooperation, and build a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity. Xinhua News Agency: We noted that recently Saudi National Security Advisor Mosaad bin Mohammad Al-Aiban and Deputy Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Ali Bagheri Kani were in China at the same time. What is China’s view on Saudi Arabia-Iran relations and the situation in the Middle East and Gulf region? Mao Ning: A few days ago, Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs Wang Yi met with Saudi and Iranian national security officials respectively in Beijing to have in-depth exchanges of views on the situation in the Middle East and Gulf region. China believes that stability in the Middle East and Gulf region bears on not only the well-being of countries and people in the region, but also international energy supply and world peace and security. Amid escalating tensions in the Middle East, China is ready to step up communication and dialogue with Saudi Arabia, Iran and other regional countries. The pressing priority is to avoid resumption of conflicts in the Middle East, which will inflict great suffering on the people in the region. China will continue to follow the guidance of the initiatives and propositions put forward by President Xi Jinping on promoting peace and security in the Middle East, uphold an objective and fair position, support Iran and the U.S. in resolving disputes through negotiations, promote the political settlement of the Yemen issue, and facilitate efforts to seek a proper and comprehensive settlement on the opening of the Strait of Hormuz. It is our hope that regional countries will uphold the principles of mutual respect and good-neighborliness, jointly create a new regional architecture for common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security, and realize lasting peace in the region. Both Saudi Arabia and Iran highly commended President Xi Jinping’s initiatives and propositions on promoting peace and security in the Middle East, expressed the willingness to maintain dialogue and communication with various parties in the spirit of the Beijing Agreement, and welcomed China’s continued efforts to play a constructive role. China News Service: To follow up on Vice President Han Zheng’s visit to Georgia you just announced, could you share the background and program? What are China’s expectations for the visit? Mao Ning: China and Georgia are comprehensive strategic partners. In recent years, guided by the blueprint mapped out by leaders of the two countries, bilateral relations have grown rapidly, with cooperation in various fields yielding fruitful outcomes. During this visit, Vice President Han Zheng will exchange views with the Georgian leadership on bilateral ties and issues of mutual interest. China stands ready to work with the Georgian side to fully implement the important common understandings reached by leaders of the two sides, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, and maintain the sustained growth of bilateral relations for the benefit of both peoples. AFP: According to reporting by the Financial Times, officials in Beijing, Moscow and Washington have been working to schedule talks between the three presidents on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen. Can the Chinese foreign ministry confirm this? Mao Ning: China is in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state. Phoenix TV: It’s reported that on November 3, Britain’s National Cyber Security Centre, which is part of the Government Communications Headquarters, issued the annual report on cybersecurity, saying that China is a leading developer of AI-cyber capability. By 2028, it is “highly likely” that China will routinely use AI-cyber to carry out hacking activities, which represents the “most sophisticated and sustained” cyber challenge facing the UK. What’s your comment? Mao Ning: We noted the relevant reports. China expresses grave concern over the wanton speculative accusation brought by the UK despite the absence of evidence. AI-generated cybersecurity risks are a global challenge and require new rules formulated at the UN to form a global response. Regrettably, the UK, having long politicized the cybersecurity issue, is now rehashing hacking allegations as a pretext to curb China’s AI development. This type of action is not helpful for increasing mutual trust between China and the UK, and hurts the UK’s credibility when it comes to cooperation on global AI security governance. China believes that the development of AI should be open and for progress, for good and for all, aim at both security and advancement, and ensure it is safe, reliable and controllable.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on November 3, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-03
The ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) will be held in Shanghai from November 5 to 10. Upon invitation, leaders from foreign countries, including Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, Austrian Federal Chancellor Christian Stocker, Liberian Vice President Jeremiah Koung, Cuban Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Trade and Investment Oscar Pérez-Oliva Fraga, Slovak Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economy Denisa Sakova, and Georgian Vice Prime Minister and Minister of Economy and Sustainable Development Mariam Kvrivishvili, will attend the opening ceremony of the CIIE and related events. China Daily: The 2026 World Internet Conference has just opened in Wuzhen. This year’s theme is “Open Source and Openness, Joint Contribution and Shared Benefits—Jointly Building a Community with a Shared Future in Cyberspace.” Discussions will focus on cutting-edge and hot topics in the digital intelligent age, especially on AI development practices and governance concepts. Premier Li Qiang attended the opening ceremony and delivered keynote remarks. Could you share more details? The age of AI has also brought risks such as the abuse of technology, the digital divide, and the overstretched concept of security. What’s China’s view on this? Mao Ning: As Premier Li Qiang pointed out in the remarks, despite rapid technological advances, one major question of common concern remains unchanged: how can the Internet better benefit humanity? At the 2015 World Internet Conference, President Xi Jinping put forward the vision of building a community with a shared future in cyberspace, offering a Chinese approach to Internet development and governance. The ultimate purpose of Internet development must be to promote people’s all-round development. Greater emphasis needs to be placed on a people-centered value orientation. Internet-related technologies should enhance people’s capabilities, expand their choices, affirm human worth, and improve their well-being—rather than make people subordinate to technology, still less allow technology to exacerbate divisions in human development. For the international community to jointly build a community with a shared future in cyberspace, we should harness the power of technology to open new grounds for development. China will continue to pursue open innovation, promote technology transfer and knowledge sharing, and work with all to build an open, inclusive and dynamic global ecosystem for digital innovation. We should ensure credibility and controllability to strengthen the shields of digital security. China will respect the legitimate cybersecurity concerns of all countries, work with all to confront security challenges, and oppose erecting digital iron curtains. We should pursue universally beneficial and balanced development to promote the sharing of digital dividends. China will actively implement the Global Development Initiative and support the Global South countries in building digital infrastructure and enhancing digital capacity. We should advance open dialogue to improve the multilateral governance system. China will act on the principle of extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit, and promote more just and equitable global Internet governance. China-Arab TV: Sultan Haitham of Oman paid a state visit to China. Could you share more information on it? Mao Ning: During the visit, President Xi Jinping and Sultan Haitham had in-depth exchanges on China-Oman relations and issues of mutual interest, reaching important common understandings. The two heads of state made top-level plans for the next-stage development of bilateral ties. Premier Li Qiang held comprehensive discussions with Sultan Haitham on scaling up cooperation in various fields between the two countries. China has released information on the relevant events of the visit, which you can refer to. China will work with the Omani side to act on the important common understandings reached by the two heads of state and jointly elevate our strategic partnership to a new height. Asahi Shimbun: This year’s APEC Ministerial Meeting will be held via video conference. What is the reason for holding the meeting virtually this year? Mao Ning: As the host of APEC 2026, China attaches high importance to holding the APEC Ministerial Meeting. Taking into account all relevant factors, it has been decided that this year’s APEC Ministerial Meeting will be held via video conference to ensure optimal effects. We are confident that with the concerted efforts of all parties, the Ministerial Meeting will achieve positive outcomes and make good preparations for the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. Reuters: Foreign Minister Wang Yi has met with the Iranian and Saudi national security officials yesterday discussing the Middle East conflict. Was China able to bring the Iranian and Saudi officials into the same room for a trilateral meeting? And if not, does China plan to do that? Mao Ning: Recently, Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs Wang Yi met with Saudi and Iranian national security officials respectively in Beijing. We have released information on the meetings. You may refer to the readouts. China stands ready to continue making active efforts to promote dialogue and deescalation. Kyodo News: Director of the International Department of the Workers’ Party of Korea Central Committee Kim Song Nam is in Beijing today on a visit. Which Chinese officials have met with him? Mao Ning: I do not have any information. Reuters: To follow up on Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s meeting with the Iranian and Saudi officials, we are also aware that the Oman delegation was in Beijing yesterday at the same time. Was there any opportunity for them to meet with the Saudi and Iranian security officials? Was China open to providing a space for that? Mao Ning: We have released the readouts of the visits. China is always ready to play its role in promoting dialogue and communication. AFP: Also just to follow up on the visits by Iranian and Saudi officials to China, under this context, is China at all concerned about a possible resumption of U.S. or Israeli attacks on Iran after the U.S. midterm elections? Mao Ning: Director Wang Yi has elaborated on China’s position on the situation in the Middle East and the Gulf region. China believes that military means are not the solution. They will only lead to escalation that serves no one’s interest. It is hoped that relevant parties will stick to peace, resolve disputes through dialogue and negotiation, and restore peace and tranquility in the Middle East and the Gulf region at an early date. Bloomberg: It’s reported that Russian defense minister is on a visit to China. We are wondering if the foreign ministry can confirm this. Mao Ning: I have no information to share at the moment. AFP: The Financial Times has reported that NVIDIA has told some of its data center partners that they must sell at least 51 percent of their services to non-Chinese companies going forward, which may restrict Chinese firms’ access to key technology used in AI. What is China’s reaction to this? Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with the specifics. We believe that all parties should engage in cooperation based on the principles of fairness, transparency and non-discrimination.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on November 2, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
At the invitation of President Xi Jinping, President of the Gabonese Republic Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema will pay a state visit to China from November 3 to 7. Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi and Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao will co-chair the 37th APEC Ministerial Meeting via video conference in Beijing on November 3. Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi will chair the 11th Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Beijing from November 3 to 4. Xinhua News Agency: To follow up on your announcement about Gabon’s President Nguema’s upcoming visit to China, can you share the arrangements and China’s expectation of the visit? How does China view its relations with Gabon? Mao Ning: This will be President Nguema’s first state visit to China since he took office. During the visit, President Xi Jinping will hold a welcome ceremony and a welcome banquet for President Nguema. The two heads of state will hold talks. Premier Li Qiang and Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee Zhao Leji will meet with him respectively. President Nguema will also attend the ninth China International Import Expo and visit Shanghai. China and Gabon are comprehensive strategic cooperative partners that enjoy traditional friendship and mutual trust. Over the past 52 years of diplomatic relations, the two countries have supported and helped each other, engaged in fruitful practical cooperation in various fields, and had close coordination and collaboration on multilateral affairs. Through the visit, China stands ready to work with Gabon to elevate bilateral relations to a new height and make greater contributions to building an all-weather China-Africa community with a shared future for the new era. Yonhap News Agency: It’s reported that the DPRK on October 31 announced that it conducted a test of a cluster warhead for tactical ballistic missile. The test violates UN Security Council resolutions concerning the DPRK, and comes at a time when the ROK has proposed military talks, which the DPRK has yet to respond. What’s China’s comment on the DPRK’s test launch? Mao Ning: China noted the relevant report and the fact that the DPRK has recently expressed its position on multiple occasions regarding the military activities by the U.S., the ROK and Japan. We hope the relevant parties will face up to the root cause of the Korean Peninsula issue, stick to the direction of political settlement, and make efforts to ease tensions and maintain peace and stability in the region. Yonhap News Agency: The FBI said on October 31 that the DPRK was behind the hacking of Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, in which about US$ 6.3 billion was stolen. U.S. President Trump said he would discuss the matter with the DPRK if the allegations are confirmed. What is China’s view on this incident and President Trump’s related remarks? Mao Ning: We are not familiar with that. CGTN: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin just concluded their visits to China. How does China assess the outcomes of the two visits? What’s China’s expectation of China-Germany relations and China-Switzerland relations moving forward? Mao Ning: This is President Steinmeier’s first state visit to China in eight years, and the first visit by a Swiss president to China in seven years. President Xi Jinping held talks with President Steinmeier and met with President Parmelin. President Xi and President Steinmeier noted that as the world’s second and third largest economies, China and Germany should shoulder the responsibility for safeguarding world peace and development and striving for a more just and equitable global governance system. Both sides spoke highly of the fruitful outcomes of China-Germany relations, and agreed to uphold mutual respect and equality, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, deepen people-to-people exchanges, and properly handle differences through dialogue and consultation, so as to usher in a new chapter of China-Germany all-round strategic partnership. President Xi and President Parmelin agreed to respect each other’s core interests, consolidate political mutual trust, make good use of the dialogue mechanisms in various fields, deepen collaboration on bilateral and multilateral affairs, champion multilateralism and free trade, and elevate China-Switzerland relations to a new height. The two presidents witnessed the signing of the Protocol Enhancing the Free Trade Agreement between China and Switzerland and other cooperation documents, including on scientific research, labor and employment, and media. Today, changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world, and the dimension of change and turbulence is becoming more prominent. The two presidents’ visits to China have sent out a positive message of strengthening communication and coordination, deepening open cooperation, and supporting multilateralism and free trade, and set a sound example for the growth of China-EU relations. China will work with various parties to focus on cooperation and mutual benefits, and inject more certainty into the stability and prosperity in today’s world. Shenzhen TV: Could you share the background of the 11th Lancang-Mekong Cooperation (LMC) Foreign Ministers’ Meeting? As the host, what are China’s expectations for the event? Mao Ning: This year marks the 10th anniversary of the first LMC Leaders’ Meeting. Over the past decade, with the concerted efforts of all countries, LMC has grown from strength to strength, becoming a stellar example of regional cooperation brimming with vitality and potential. Solid progress has been made in building a community with a shared future between China and the five Mekong countries bilaterally and multilaterally. Trade between the two sides has exceeded US$500 billion, up by 150 percent compared with that of 10 years ago. Efforts in building the LMC Economic Development Belt have yielded fruitful outcomes. The Lancang-Mekong Innovation Corridor has become a new highlight. Faster headway is being made in boosting regional power connectivity. The LMC Special Fund has provided support for over 1,000 small and smart projects. The Lancang-Mekong Sweet Spring Action and the Hundred, Thousand, Ten Thousand Action Plan on Lancang-Mekong Agricultural Cooperation, among others, have delivered real results. The Lancang-Mekong Visa has facilitated people-to-people exchanges among the six countries. As the century-defining transformation unfolds at an accelerating pace, LMC’s role in promoting openness and development and safeguarding peace and tranquility is becoming even more pronounced. China hopes to take the upcoming Foreign Ministers’ Meeting as an opportunity to work with the five Mekong countries to take stock of past experience, plan future cooperation, discuss in particular the blueprint for LMC 2.0, explore new mechanisms for openness and cooperation, build more platforms for industrial innovation, and make greater progress in law enforcement and security cooperation, so as to inject strong impetus into building a Lancang-Mekong community with a shared future of peace, prosperity and sustainable development. People’s Daily: On October 31 Beijing time, the Committee on Disarmament and International Security (First Committee) of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly adopted the resolution “Promoting international cooperation on peaceful uses in the context of international security” tabled by China. Could you share more details? Mao Ning: We welcome the adoption by the First Committee of the resolution “Promoting international cooperation on peaceful uses in the context of international security.” The resolution calls for efforts to coordinate both development and security, strengthen the role of the UN, and safeguard developing countries’ lawful rights to peaceful uses of technology. The resolution urges all countries to take concrete actions to promote international cooperation on peaceful uses, and avoid maintaining restrictions incompatible with their international obligations. The resolution also decides to continue consideration of the relevant issue at the UN General Assembly. This is the fourth time for China to submit the resolution on peaceful uses of technology to the UN General Assembly since 2021, which has received broad support from the international community. Acting on the resolution is an important step for China to implement the Global Security Initiative. We will work with various parties to promote the full and effective implementation of the resolution and make sure that progress in technology will further contribute to peace and development for humanity. Global Times: The Spokesperson said a few days ago that China will send special envoys to the Middle East, the Gulf region, the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa. Can you share more details? Mao Ning: To deliver on the initiatives and propositions put forward by President Xi Jinping on promoting peace and security in the Middle East and the four principles on the constructive participation of relevant parties in the resolution of African hotspot issues, Special Envoy of the Chinese Government on the Middle East Issue Zhai Jun will visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia in early and mid-November; Special Representative of the Chinese Government on African Affairs Liu Xianfa will visit Ethiopia, Djibouti and Egypt in early and mid-November; and Special Envoy for the Horn of Africa Affairs of the Foreign Ministry Hu Changchun will visit Eritrea in early November. These shuttle diplomacy visits in this period of time by Chinese special envoys and special representative are aimed at promoting peace talks, easing tensions, and playing a constructive role in upholding regional peace and stability.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson’s Remarks on the 7.6 Magnitude Earthquake in Panama
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Q: It’s reported that a 7.6 magnitude earthquake struck Panama on October 10, followed by over 100 aftershocks. What is China’s comment? A: China expresses sympathies to the Panamanian government and people in the affected region. As of now, there is no report of casualties involving Chinese nationals in the earthquake. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Chinese Embassy in Panama will continue to closely monitor the situation and promptly provide necessary assistance to Chinese nationals in need. We remind Chinese nationals in Panama to take precautions against secondary hazards caused by the earthquake.
